routes.description: Establish that humans are personally accountable under a trustworthy divine moral order, that judgment answers genuine guilt, and that Christ's substitutionary death and resurrection make merciful salvation coherent through repentance and faith.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if divine authority and human culpability are adequately grounded, punishment and substitution are shown to be morally intelligible, and repentance, faith, grace, and resurrection form a coherent account of salvation.

motionBridge.description: Connect the account of sin, judgment, atonement, and salvation into a morally and explanatorily coherent gospel.

centralBridges.description: Ground God's moral authority and show that human beings bear personal guilt for their own wrongdoing.
Explain why judgment is deserved and how Christ's substitution permits mercy without abandoning justice.
Specify how repentance, faith, grace, resurrection, and personal transformation provide salvation rather than moral works.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Supply a warrant for trusting God, scripture, creation, conscience, and claimed transformative experience.
Reconcile divine foreknowledge and a fallen creation with individual responsibility and confidence in divine justice.

routes.description: Show that the gospel account fails moral or explanatory scrutiny because responsibility is misassigned, substitution does not resolve wrongdoing, divine alternatives appear less harmful, and its foundational and salvific claims lack reliable evidential support.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if central features of guilt, judgment, atonement, or salvation are shown to be unjustified, internally unstable, needlessly designed, or dependent on methods that cannot reliably establish their truth.

motionBridge.description: Demonstrate that the proposed account of sin, atonement, and salvation does not jointly satisfy moral and explanatory standards.

centralBridges.description: Test whether inherited guilt and an omniscient creator's choices are compatible with personal culpability and just punishment.
Test whether sacrificial substitution is necessary, morally permissible, and capable of addressing defective character or repeated wrongdoing.
Require non-circular, discriminating support for God, scripture, resurrection, and the claimed operation of salvation.
Compare the gospel's history of suffering, hiddenness, judgment, and rescue with less harmful divine alternatives.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Determine whether conversion and salvation claims permit adverse experience to count against them.
Distinguish evidence-proportioned confidence from faith, assertion, assumed design, and appeals to humility.

sections.title: Human Guilt, Divine Foreknowledge, and Responsibility
sections.rationale: The justice of sin and judgment depends on whether people are accountable for their conduct despite inherited conditions, divine foreknowledge, creative choice, and the availability of alternative worlds.

sections.title: Substitutionary Atonement, Forgiveness, and Moral Repair
sections.rationale: This issue directly tests whether Christ's sacrifice is necessary and just, whether penalty payment can ground forgiveness, and whether substitution addresses the wrongdoer's underlying moral condition.

sections.title: Evidence for God, Scripture, and Resurrection
sections.rationale: The gospel's explanation requires support for its divine lawgiver, scriptural authority, and resurrection claims, making the dispute over creation, revelation, faith, and evidential standards structurally central.

sections.title: Repentance, Faith, Conversion, and the Salvation Promise
sections.rationale: The account must explain how salvation is obtained and known while addressing whether failed conversion, continued nonbelief, or contrary experience can meaningfully test its promises.

sections.title: Suffering, Divine Hiddenness, and the Design of Judgment
sections.rationale: The moral and explanatory adequacy of the gospel also turns on whether a fallen world, divine absence, severe suffering, and ultimate punishment fit a wise and just salvific plan.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-01.proposition: God's moral law establishes human guilt, while Jesus's death pays the guilty person's penalty and thereby permits a judge to forgive without abandoning justice.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-03.proposition: The gospel becomes intelligible when a person humbly acknowledges serious sin, repents, and trusts the risen Christ for eternal life as God's gift.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-09.proposition: God has supplied moral knowledge through a divinely given conscience whose operation persists despite social shaping and the possibility that it becomes seared.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: Divine foreknowledge and original sin do not excuse personal wrongdoing, just as blaming God would not remove a guilty defendant's responsibility for a serious crime.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-05.proposition: A former profession of Christianity followed by departure does not disconfirm the gospel's promise if the person never genuinely repented and therefore underwent a false conversion.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-07.proposition: The existence of creation is self-evident evidence of a creator in the same way that a building or painting evidences its maker.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-06.proposition: Pervasive suffering, disease, natural disaster, and death corroborate the biblical teaching that humanity inhabits a fallen creation.

chunk-004:chunk004-candidate-02.proposition: Christianity treats people as guilty before a holy judge and offers salvation through divine mercy made legally possible by Christ's sacrificial death and resurrection rather than by good works.

chunk-004:chunk004-candidate-03.proposition: Sinners deserve the loss imposed at judgment, and where human reason cannot resolve the severity of that outcome, God's righteousness warrants trust that he will act justly.

chunk-004:chunk004-candidate-05.proposition: Belief in the resurrection is warranted by experiential revelation from the living Christ, which is promised to those who repent, obey, and trust Christ as their sin-bearer.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-04.proposition: Original sin cannot fairly be assigned to humanity if an omniscient God knowingly chose a creation in which human disobedience was inevitable despite having alternatives.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-05.proposition: Inherited sin is morally incoherent because it assigns people guilt and punishment for conduct committed by other people before they were born.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-06.proposition: Jesus's sacrifice is an unnecessary blood ritual because a rule-making and enforcing God could forgive without requiring a sacrifice of himself to himself.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-07.proposition: A wise and powerful God seeking fellowship could create suitable people with him directly, making the history of suffering, damnation, and rescue needlessly inefficient.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-08.proposition: If earthly life is intended to teach people, God's absence makes it inferior to instruction by an available teacher and therefore evidence of a poorly designed plan.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-10.proposition: A scriptural assertion about another person's inner knowledge cannot override that person's contrary report or independently establish the assertion's truth.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-06.proposition: A former Christian's present disbelief does not show that the former belief was insincere, and reclassifying that belief as false does not establish Christianity's truth.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-05.proposition: Faith cannot demonstrate God, divine lawgiving, or scriptural truth and therefore is not a reliable method for establishing the gospel's foundational claims.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-09.proposition: Paying another person's debt can remove an obligation but does not repair the wrongdoer's defective character or prevent that person from repeating the wrongdoing.

chunk-004:chunk004-candidate-06.proposition: The promised path to belief is insulated from failure when every sincere seeker who remains unconvinced can be blamed for seeking incorrectly or hardening their heart.
